column2: Mix the chicken with the yoghurt, paprika and thyme and marinate in the fridge for 1 hour; then wash your hands.
Scrub the potato well in its skin and cut into wedges.
Arrange the chicken and potatoes spaced out on the tray and bake for 40 minutes, turning halfway.
Chicken must reach 74°C inside; no pink should remain near the bone.
When lukewarm, remove all the meat from the bone; check for small bones and gristle.
Break into small pieces the child can chew.
Add the grated carrot and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the tomato sauce; cook over low heat for 5 minutes.
Mix with the drained pasta.
Place the cheese and tomato between the slices of bread.
Toast in a sandwich maker for 3 minutes until the cheese melts.
Melted cheese stays very hot inside; don't serve until it has cooled.
Cool for 5 minutes and cut into four.
Dice the carrot and courgette small; wash the rice.
Melt the butter in a pan and stir the vegetables for 3 minutes.
Add the rice and water; cook over low heat for 20 minutes until the rice is soft.
Leave it chunky; this develops chewing skills.
Melt the butter in a pan and soften the potato with 2 spoonfuls of water, covered, for 10 minutes.
Break the broccoli into small florets; cut the carrot into thin sticks.
Toss the vegetables with olive oil and spread on the tray; place the salmon in the middle.
Drizzle with the lemon and flake the salmon; serve lukewarm with the vegetables.
Heat the olive oil in a pan and stir the vegetables for 3 minutes.
Add the boiled borlotti beans and water; cook covered over low heat for 20 minutes.
Mash the beans lightly with a fork.
Dried pulses can cause wind in little ones; if giving for the first time, start with a small portion.
Peel and dice the potatoes and boil for 15 minutes until soft.
Add the peas and carrot and cook for 5 minutes; no pink should remain in the mince.
Drain the potatoes and mash smooth with the milk using a fork.
Spread the mince mixture in the dish first, then the mash on top; sprinkle with the cheese.
Bake for 15 minutes until golden on top.
Wash the lentils; chop the carrot small.
Bring the lentils, carrot and water to the boil; skim off the foam.
Cook over low heat for 20 minutes until the lentils break down.
Wash and finely chop the spinach; add and cook for 3 minutes.
Blend; add the butter.
Preheat the oven to 190°C; line a small ovenproof dish with baking paper.
Grate the courgette and carrot and squeeze out the liquid well with your hands.
Mix the vegetables, egg, flour and curd cheese.
Spread the mixture in the dish 1.5 cm thick.
Bake for 25 minutes until golden on top and firm in the middle.
Rest for 10 minutes and cut into sticks the child can hold.
Melt the butter in a pan and stir the rice in it for 1 minute.
Add the chicken stock and peas; when it boils, cook covered over low heat for 15 minutes.
Finely shred the boiled chicken and add it.
Wash the strawberries and remove the stalks; peel and slice the banana.
Blend the yoghurt, banana and strawberries until smooth.
Pour into moulds and freeze for at least 4 hours.
Take out 5 minutes before serving; they come out of the mould easily.
Don't refreeze ice lollies that have thawed.
Knead the mince and breadcrumbs; make walnut-sized, slightly flat meatballs and wash your hands.
Heat the olive oil in a pan and brown the meatballs for 3 minutes on each side.
Add the grated tomato and 3 spoonfuls of water; cook covered over low heat for 10 minutes.
Halve the meatballs and serve with rice.
Grate the courgette and squeeze out the liquid; chop the corn finely.
Spread the cheese, courgette and corn on half of the flatbread; fold the other half over.
Cook in a dry non-stick pan over medium heat for 2 minutes on each side until the cheese melts.
Cool for 5 minutes and cut into triangles.
Mix the oats, apple, egg, milk and cinnamon and leave for 10 minutes.
Dice the meat small and trim off fat and sinew; dice the carrot small.
Cook the meat in a pan for 10 minutes until its juices are absorbed.
Add the tomato paste and carrot and stir for 2 minutes.
Add the peas and water; cook covered over low heat for 25 minutes until the meat is tender.
Pull the meat into small shreds; mash the peas lightly.
Whisk the egg, flour and milk until smooth; leave for 5 minutes.
Squeeze the boiled spinach well, chop finely and mix with the curd cheese.
Heat a non-stick pan over low heat, pour in a ladle of batter and spread it.
When cooked underneath, turn and cook 1 more minute.
Spread the spinach and curd cheese over the crepe and roll up.
Cut into slices the child can hold.
When lukewarm, add the carrot, egg yolk and breadcrumbs and knead.
Make walnut-sized flat patties and arrange on the tray.
Bake for 20 minutes until golden underneath.
Wash the courgettes and halve them; scoop out the insides with a spoon, leaving a 0.5 cm shell.
Mix the bulgur, grated tomato, olive oil and finely chopped courgette flesh.
Fill the courgettes loosely; the bulgur swells as it cooks.
Arrange in a pan and add hot water halfway up.
Cook covered over low heat for 30 minutes until the courgettes are soft and the bulgur is cooked.
When lukewarm, cut the courgettes into small pieces and serve with yoghurt.
Pour into a bowl and sprinkle with the oats.
Serve immediately with a spoon.
Dice the carrot and potato small and add them to the stock; cook for 10 minutes.
Return the chicken to the pan and heat for 1 minute.
Chop the pepper and courgette very finely.
Whisk the eggs, milk, vegetables and cheese.
Pour into the dish and bake for 20 minutes until completely set in the middle.
Rest for 5 minutes and cut into slices the child can hold.
